summary: An underground station in the heart of Technoparc Montréal, a science and technology park with 100+ companies and over 7,000 employees, surrounded by protected wetlands of the Parc-nature des Sources. It is not open yet: it will open together with the YUL-Aéroport-Montréal-Trudeau station, targeted for late 2027. The REM turns a car-dependent office/lab park into a transit-served employment hub, but development here is commercial/industrial and constrained by conservation, not residential.

notes: Station not open as of Nov 2026: dynamic tests began Aug 8-9, 2026 and high-speed automatic tests reached Marie-Curie on Oct 17, 2026; opening (with the airport station, built by ADM) remains targeted for late 2027 (rem.info, Oct 22, 2026). Opening was originally announced for 2023. Construction briefly halted in late Oct 2026 when contractor NouvLR's RBQ licence was suspended; work resumed Oct 26, 2026 (CityNews/Canadian Press: https://montreal.citynews.ca/2026/10/26/construction-rem-station-airport-resumes/). The Broccolini sites are marketing listings, not announced projects; I could not confirm their exact walking distance (a JLL listing for a Broccolini lot at Marie-Curie/Alfred-Nobel said ±600 m from the station). Cologix MTL8 is in Technoparc but I did not verify its exact address relative to the station. Coordinates are from the OpenStreetMap node for the station under construction (node 7350710746); Wikipedia gives 45°28′46″N 73°45′36″W, which matches closely. No residential projects found: the Technoparc is an employment zone and much of the remaining land is being protected (Parc-nature des Sources).

area: Pointe-Claire / Dollard-des-Ormeaux / Dorval (boul. des Sources at A-40)
summary: A station on the A-40 at boulevard des Sources, where Pointe-Claire, Dorval and Dollard-des-Ormeaux meet. The area is mostly big-box retail (Mégacentre Des Sources), light industry and strip malls. The REM is triggering the first mid-rise rental buildings: a 393-unit complex is already built just north on Brunswick, and Pointe-Claire approved a 12-storey building on the Bar-B-Barn site in 2026.

projects.description: A 12-storey rental building replacing the Bar-B-Barn restaurant at the corner of Des Sources and Brunswick, inside the Des Sources REM TOD area, with about 10% of units meeting CMHC affordability criteria and ~221 parking spaces plus car-sharing.

projects.description: Three rental buildings (130, 116 and 147 units) replacing a strip mall at Brunswick and Davignon, with rooftop pool, gym and coworking; the developer markets it as walking distance to the Des Sources REM station.

plans.name: Dollard-des-Ormeaux Urban Planning Program (Des Sources TOD area)

notes: The 3300 Des Sources renders come from an Agora Montréal forum page (enthusiast site, not official); no official project page found. Before permits are issued it still needs DDO's sign-off on infrastructure and a City–developer affordability agreement, and the City of Montréal executive committee approved its conformity on Oct 7, 2026. Sources disagree on Westwalk DDO's height: Agora lists 13/8/8 storeys, while adresses.ca says 11 storeys. The 393-unit total is consistent across sources. Westwalk is in DDO, a few hundred metres north of the station; I did not measure the exact walking distance. Pointe-Claire's new urban plan is expected by end-2026 or early 2027.

area: Pointe-Claire city centre (CF Fairview Pointe-Claire) / east Kirkland
summary: The station sits next to CF Fairview Pointe-Claire, the West Island's main shopping mall, and its bus terminal. The city's 2017-2018 City Centre SPP designated the area for transit-oriented densification. The flagship proposal, Cadillac Fairview's towers on the mall parking lot, has been frozen since 2022 by Pointe-Claire's interim control by-law and is tied up in court along with the contested Fairview Forest. Nearby, Prével's Village Lacey Green in Kirkland is under construction, and a 361-unit Westwalk rental project is rising on Saint-Jean.

The advocacy group MARE says the October 2020 proposal included about 5,000 condos, businesses and hotels. notes: Cadillac Fairview status: as of Feb 2025 its court challenges against Pointe-Claire (Mu1 and Mu2) and the CMM (Mu2) were unresolved. In Jan 2026 the Court of Québec upheld a citizen's access-to-information win against Cadillac Fairview. I found no 2026 report that the freeze on the mall lot has been lifted. Pointe-Claire's new urban plan is expected by end-2026 or early 2027 (Council, Sept 8, 2026). The Fairview Forest unit count (≈5,000 condos) comes only from an advocacy group (MARE, https://mouvementmare.org/nos-campagnes-daction/appui-sauvons-la-foret-fairview/); I did not see it on an official page. Its renders link goes to Cadillac Fairview's parking-lot project site, since there is no public Mu2 render page. Lacey Green unit counts vary by source: ~1,100 (TGTA), ~1,200 (RENX), and 950 + 111 + 47 (Global News, Nov 2025). TGTA's page says the site is next to the 'Kirkland REM station', but Prével and Global News place it near Fairview–Pointe-Claire, which matches the geography. Westwalk Pointe-Claire's renders page is a leasing site, and its walking distance to the station is my estimate (~1 km, unverified).

area: Kirkland (Centre RioCan Kirkland, rue Jean-Yves / chemin Sainte-Marie)
summary: The highest station on the REM, about 24 m above ground. It sits beside the A-40 at the south edge of the aging Centre RioCan Kirkland strip mall and next to single-family neighbourhoods; the TOD zone currently averages only about 6 homes per hectare. In 2025 Kirkland adopted a station-area special planning program (PPU) and rezoned the 15.5 ha RioCan site for a mixed-use district of 6-14 storey buildings near the station. No construction has been announced yet.

plans.name: Special Planning Program "REM Station – Town of Kirkland" (By-law 90-54-11)
Le REM à Kirkland (station info, parking)

notes: The PPU sets planning capacity, not a confirmed unit count. Broccolini said in 2020-21 that at least 1,000 homes were possible, and in July 2024 it expected construction could start in 2025 once zoning was final. I found no evidence of construction starting by Nov 2026, so status 'approved' refers only to the zoning/PPU framework. There is no official render page; the renders link is a RENX article showing a RioCan image of the proposal. The adoption table in By-law 90-54-11 lists adoption on July 7, 2025, and a certificate of compliance and coming into force on Nov 3, 2025. Sotramont's Livéo Kirkland (7 storeys, rental, at Saint-Charles / Sainte-Marie, under construction in 2026) is in Kirkland but roughly a 30-40 minute walk from the station, so I left it out. A planned footbridge over the A-40 to the Grand parc de l'Ouest and a bus/active-transport corridor on the old A-440 right-of-way are mentioned on Wikipedia, citing the Gazette and CTV, but I did not verify their current status.

area: Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue (chemin Sainte-Marie, near Senneville / Grand parc de l'Ouest)
summary: The western terminus of the REM, a ground-level station on chemin Sainte-Marie with a bus terminal, a 200-space park-and-ride and the West Island maintenance centre. Its main role is access to nature: it is the gateway to the Anse-à-l'Orme nature park and the 3,100-ha Grand parc de l'Ouest, Canada's largest municipal park. Nearby urban development is limited to a long-term eco-employment and housing plan for Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue's Secteur Nord.

plans.name: Draft Plan d'urbanisme PR-863 (renews PPU Secteur Nord and PPU Anciens-Combattants)
Stratégie de mise en valeur du Grand parc de l'Ouest (to 2050)

notes: Little real-estate activity here: no specific private development projects near the station turned up. The Provencher_Roy concept (2019) was a competition proposal, so it may not reflect current intentions. French Wikipedia, citing a CIMA+ traffic study, says the Secteur Nord PPU plans about 270 homes, 35,000 sq ft of retail and 450,000 sq ft of offices; I did not see those numbers in a primary source. I did not confirm whether draft urban plan PR-863 (public consultation notice Sept 2024) has been formally adopted. The Montréal page says a new trail from the Anse-à-l'Orme entrance runs to Cap-Saint-Jacques; the '≈3 km from the station' figure comes from Radio-Canada (Aug 2025). The nearby Cap-Nature housing project in Pierrefonds-Ouest was dropped in favour of the park, and its developers are suing for ≈$180M (Radio-Canada).
